subject: Re: SLA uplift and escalation coverage — proposed concession roadmap
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya@horizonai.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Horizon AI Legal <legal@horizonai.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA uplift request and pricing clarity

Hi Logan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran a quick internal review of risk and observed a few gaps in our requirements vs. the standard Redwood SLA: notably a 99.99% uptime target, a 15-minute critical-response window for severity 1 incidents, and named escalation coverage during regional maintenance windows.

Can you share a proposal that:
- Maps Redwood's existing uptime tiers to our needs 
- Shows retainer/retained on-call options (hours and estimated monthly cost)
- Outlines any discounts for a 12-month commit at our expected monthly throughput (~4M tokens/mo)

I attached a small snapshot of our Q2 usage to help size the commit. We are aiming to decide by EOW.

Best,
Priya
Head of Platform Ops — Horizon AI

----

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@horizonai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA uplift request and pricing clarity

Hi Priya —

Thanks for the clear ask and the usage snapshot, very helpful. High-level response up front: we can support a 99.99% uptime SLO with a dedicated commit and a retained on-call retainer that guarantees a 15-minute critical-response window for sev-1. There are a few levers to balance cost vs. guarantees: dedicated reserved capacity vs. regional failover, and whether you want 24/7 named escalation or a shared rapid-response pod.

Attached is a draft term sheet (SLA_Uplift_Term_Sheet.pdf) that outlines three options:
1) Standard Plus: 99.95% uptime, 1-hour sev-1 response, no named oncall (lowest uplift)
2) Assured: 99.99% uptime, 15-minute sev-1 response, retained on-call (staffed by a small named roster during your peak hours)
3) Critical Guard: 99.995% uptime, 15-minute response, 24/7 named escalation + quarterly tabletop drills (highest uplift)

For a 12-month commit at ~4M tokens/mo we can provide:
- 12% list discount on hosted usage for Assured (option 2) if Horizon commits to a $Xk/mo baseline and a 6-month ramp schedule
- If you opt for Dedicated (reserved GPUs) we can increase that to 16% and include one free failover test per year

Short ask: can you confirm whether Horizon expects to run in multi-region (preferred) or single-region? That will change the estimate for the dedicated capacity uplift.

I'll loop Ben and Marissa to align on pricing guardrails and legal. Happy to jump on a quick call today.

Thanks,
Logan
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference

----

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@horizonai.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA uplift request and pricing clarity (pricing sketch)

Priya —

Quick sketch on numbers to make the tradeoffs concrete (ballpark, pending usage verification):
- Assured (hosted + retained on-call): +$12k/mo uplift; 12% usage discount with 12-mo commit; includes named escalation during PST peak hours (7am–7pm PT).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity for 4M tokens): +$20–24k/mo uplift depending on right-sizing; 16% usage discount; includes one mandatory failover drill per year and on-call for full business hours.
- Dedicated + 24/7 Escalation (Critical Guard): +$34k/mo uplift; 18% discount; 24/7 named escalation and quarterly drills.

We can reduce the uplifts if Horizon takes a 24-month commit or increases baseline by 25% (better capacity amortization).

Ben
Sr. Sales — Redwood Inference

----

From: Priya Shah <priya@horizonai.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Horizon AI Legal <legal@horizonai.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Jul 2026 08:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA uplift request and pricing clarity

Thanks Logan/Ben — this is helpful. A few clarifying notes from our side: 
- We will run multi-region (primary US, secondary EU) for redundancy.
- Preferred outcome: Assured (option 2) if you can tighten the named escalation window to 24/7 on-call for sev-1 during the first 90 days (we'll transition to PST peak-only after ramp).
- Commercial ask: Horizon needs a 15% uplift discount vs. list for Assured with a 12-month commit, or we will default to Dedicated + 16% discount (but that requires longer procurement lead time).

Legal flagged two items for later negotiation: crediting calculation (how downtime is measured) and data residency guarantees for EU failover.

Can Marissa confirm whether the 15% on Assured is feasible vs. the numbers Ben shared?

Best,
Priya

----

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@horizonai.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA uplift request and pricing clarity — proposed concession

Hi Priya —

Thanks for the clear ask and for committing to multi-region; that helps a lot for availability. We ran the numbers and can meet you halfway on the commercial ask:

Proposed concession (one-time):
- Assured package at 15% usage discount for the 12-month commit if Horizon signs within 10 business days and accepts the proposed retainer structure.
- In exchange, we request a 30-day minimum notice for planned failover tests and a 90-day phased ramp schedule documented in the mutual action plan.
- For the first 90 days we will staff 24/7 named escalation for sev-1 incidents (as requested). After that, we transition to named escalation during PST peak hours per the SLA.

We will work with Legal to tighten the crediting language around measurement windows and to include an EU data residency addendum for failover only (no permanent storage in EU unless requested).

Next steps:
1) If acceptable, Horizon signs the term sheet (SLA_Uplift_Term_Sheet.pdf) and returns it to us.
2) Redwood will issue a DocuSign link for a SOW addendum and schedule a kickoff for the first failover drill.

I've attached a conservative response matrix (redwood-response-matrix.xlsx) that shows staffed coverage vs. escalation paths. Ben will create a final price quote and we can put the HubSpot deal into the approved stage.

If that works, I can have Legal send the draft addendum today.

Cheers,
Marissa
VP, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

----

Attachments referenced in thread:
- SLA_Uplift_Term_Sheet.pdf (term sheet with discrete SLOs and retainer options)
- usage_snapshot_Q2.csv (Horizon AI usage sample provided by Priya)
- redwood-response-matrix.xlsx (coverage and escalation mapping)
